method: NEW BASELINE (suffix-free; resets fullreview-delta and fullreview-full). Fable 5.1 graded every one of the 17 panel rows from scratch, one finding-verifier batch per ≤8 findings (finding-verifier agent, lean REFUTED), model identity held for graders and verifiers. headline: Seventeen rows graded from scratch on Day 0 of cycle 16 and no A- survives: 13 rows fell one notch or more from their carried-forward grades (cto A-→B+, principal A-→B+, aiq B+→B, cpo B+→B-, designer A-→B+, dataviz B+→B, narrative B+→C+, a11y A-→B+, reader B+→B-, observability A-→B+, data-architect B+→B, integrations A-→B+, devex A-→B+), 1 rose (qs C+→B-), 3 held (security, cost, growth). The delta chain had been flattering: every carried grade came from a run that measured a change surface, and a from-scratch look at the whole product on its emptiest day is a harsher instrument by design. The review earned its keep the same night: four rows independently found that the chronicle auto-publish sweep had republished cycle 15's tombstoned Week-1 draft on Day 0 (#3485, repaired live within the run). 99 findings CONFIRMED, 5 PLAUSIBLE, 12 REFUTED — a 10% first-pass refutation rate against the historical ~50%; three grades moved on verifier dissent (qs, security, data-architect), recorded rather than averaged.

cto.title: CTO / architect

rubric_anchors.A: Every resilience/ops claim in ARCHITECTURE.md reproduces against live CDK + AWS state; liveness sensors are capability-verified (not just IAM-parity-verified) after deploy; no alarm sits in ALARM unexplained beyond ~72h; the ADR-103 ledger rows match live subsystem state — all inside the solo-operator $85/mo envelope with no added standing machinery.
rubric_anchors.C: The core pipeline (ingest→DLQ→digest, S3/DDB protection, per-lambda roles) works, but one or more monitoring paths are silently dead, the canonical architecture doc materially misdescribes live behavior (crons, stack ownership, quotas), and stale alarms/ledger rows accumulate with no reconcile loop.
rubric_anchors.F: Async paths without DLQ/alarm coverage, shared over-privileged IAM roles, S3/DDB unprotected against operator error, or documentation wrong enough that an incident responder acting on it would make things worse.
rubric_anchors.extension_note: EXTENDED (not redefined), per seed cto-S1: (1) the envelope in the A anchor is now the ADR-133 #2801 base of $215/mo (surge $252) effective 2026-09-01 — live Budgets limit reads 215.0, forecast $130.79, tier 0 — so 'no added standing machinery' is judged against that ceiling; (2) the A anchor additionally requires that a READER-AUDIENCE red reaches a human within one detection interval of the probe that raised it, independent of any session or wrap running — the 09-01 outage showed 'immediate detection, ~31h escalation' is not A; (3) 'unexplained' in the 72h clause now includes 'explained by a citation whose stated cause is not the alarm's current cause' — a rotted citation is worse than none for the gate that reads it.

cto.trend_note: A- (2026-08-16 delta) → B+: the prior grade predates the launch-day reader outage; this baseline reproduced that its fix (#3423) moved the escalation bar into two readers that run on a slower or inverted clock while the alarm's live routing is unchanged, found two Errors alarms structurally unable to fire on the surfaces they guard, three unreproducible resilience claims in ARCHITECTURE.md, and a lit alarm explained by a citation for a different, cured cause — against a data-protection, IAM, stack and cost posture that reproduces cleanly at the extended $215 envelope.

findings_confirmed.corrected_root_cause: Threshold copied from a function-level alarm onto a function whose failure mode is per-endpoint; an Errors-count alarm on a multi-endpoint Lambda cannot see a sub-surface outage at any threshold >1 unless it is a rate with a floor. The canary, not this alarm, is the surface's real detector — so the defect is a redundancy gap, not the sole-detector gap the P2 implied.

The handler's duplicate/stale guards make retries safe, so the gap is invisibility, not double-send.

principal.title: Principal engineer

rubric_anchors.A: Full offline suite green and fast with creds blanked; every stated quality gate (coverage floor, mypy tier set, deploy-critical lane, format gates) matches measured reality within a small tolerance; no unreferenced code shipping in the every-bundle shared modules; exactly one canonical implementation per platform invariant (float→Decimal, Pacific-date, ISO parse); golden tests pinned against the known wall-clock defect class.
rubric_anchors.C: Suite green but the gates are partly decorative — coverage floor drifted far below actual so backsliding is possible, gate comments/config contradict enforcement status, hundreds of dead lines ship in every Lambda bundle, and invariant helpers are forked with divergent edge-case semantics.
rubric_anchors.F: Red main tolerated or gates disabled to get green; tests mirror implementation so defects cannot fail them; no coverage or type gate at all; wall-clock time bombs in fixtures with no encoded lesson.
rubric_anchors.extension_note: EXTENSION (not a redefinition): A additionally requires that EVERY landing path onto main — PR merge or direct push — meets at least the pre-merge lane before the commit is on main, and that a guard which scans source (AST/regex) ships with a synthetic must-fail control. C additionally covers the case where the gates are sound in construction but the landing path most commits actually use bypasses them, so reds are measured on main rather than prevented (this run: 26 of 29 red Unit-Test runs in 14 days were direct pushes).

principal.trend_note: A- (2026-08-16) → B+: the gate estate got stronger since (measured-coverage high-water ratchet, full-suite pre-merge job, gate census with mutation verdicts, whole-surface mypy), but measured landing reality moved the other way — 29 red Unit-Test runs on main in 14 days, 26 of them via direct pushes no CI check can stop, and the same regenerated-artifact test class redding at both resets — which is the C-anchor's 'gates partly decorative' in process form rather than in construction.

aiq.title: AI-quality lead

rubric_anchors.A: Every reader-facing AI narrative passes a deterministic grounding gate with the audience-correct fail mode (fail-closed public, keep-best internal), every prompt carries the phase/day truth, a reset leaves zero wiped-cycle narrative reachable on any live endpoint, and live spot-checks find no number, date, or verdict a Day-4 reader couldn't trace to real data.
rubric_anchors.C: The grounding harness exists and covers the flagship surfaces, but coverage is convention rather than structure — at least one live surface serves stale, ungated, or mischaracterized AI content and no test or gate would catch it.
rubric_anchors.F: Models receive raw data and ship unchecked numbers or claims to readers, or a reset/budget state silently narrates wiped or fabricated history as current with no tombstone semantics at all.
rubric_anchors.extension_note: Extension (not redefinition): the A anchor's 'live spot-checks' clause is read on Day 0 as 'no claim a Day-0 reader couldn't trace' — a tense claim about a genesis that has not happened, or a cause attributed to a data absence the registry already explains (paused / lag-by-design), counts as untraceable exactly like a fabricated number. cpo.title: CPO

rubric_anchors.A: Every door's first screen states its loop role; every live engagement hook (predict-the-week, ask-the-board, chronicle/podcast cadence) is demonstrably alive-or-honestly-absent on ANY day of a cycle including Day 4 of a fresh reset; a shared bare URL lands on the page; each of the 4 audiences finds its surface within one click of Home; the early-cycle state reads as a deliberate season premiere (day counter, pre-registration, prequels, cycle-vs-cycle context).
rubric_anchors.C: Doors render and the loop is taught, but one or more engagement hooks silently serve stale or dead-cycle content, shared links 404, or the fresh-cycle state depends on the reader's forgiveness to not read as broken — returnability exists on paper but not on the calendar.
rubric_anchors.F: The early-cycle site reads as broken or dishonest: blank doors, no day counter or pre-registration, hooks dead or fabricating (gains hidden, dead weeks presented as live, chronicle inventing content beyond the logged data).
rubric_anchors.extension_note: EXTENSION (not a redefinition): 'demonstrably alive-or-honestly-absent' is read to include every artifact a hook publishes downstream of its own page — the permalink, the manifest, the 'previously on' recap memory, the share-kit, the subscriber onboarding email. A hook whose page carries an honest banner but which pushes dead-cycle content through those channels is graded at the C anchor. Also extended for the seed: 'the loop is taught' requires that the loop's protocols→data leg has at least one instrument that can grade whether coaching moved behavior; an instrument that exists but has never graded is 'dead' in the F-anchor sense, mitigated to C when the site does not claim it works.

cpo.process_verdict: CPO-1 belonged to two existing rituals and escaped both: the #2109 phase-filter ratchet (extended by #3444 two days ago) does not see chronicle_approve_lambda's raw table.query, and restart_verify (23 checks) asserts the lead-ins but never that the auto-publish window is empty of drafts post-reset — so add the ratchet member and the verify assertion, and make the publish path re-derive rather than replay a stored snapshot; the Story door then also needs its charter dead-man (a premiere-sweep check in tests/visual_qa.py that would have gone red at 18:01Z). CPO-2 belonged to observability and to the prove-it discipline: a grader that logged 'kept=0 broken=0' for 21 days had no metric and no alarm, and its only test mocked the function under test — the gate to add is the 'vacuous positive control' rule from the review-discipline index applied to every deterministic grader (a test must drive the real evaluator to a non-inconclusive verdict) plus a dead-man on every grader's output count.

B- (down from B+) is supported by one live P1 on the flagship narrative surface plus a dark coaching-evidence instrument; I would not go lower because the P1's blast radius is narrower than filed (subscribers spared by the sender's 7-day window; the recall corpus already held the installment before the sweep) and the other three are pre-start copy defects. dataviz.title: Data-viz expert

rubric_anchors.A: Every visual encoding is proportional and honest at any n (lengths/areas never anchored to arbitrary floors), every statistical claim carries visible-and-reachable n/CI on touch and keyboard, low-n charts refuse or degrade with explicit copy, and the live site renders zero contradictory encodings on any surface.
rubric_anchors.C: Charts render and mostly caption honestly, but multiple encodings exaggerate (truncated-baseline bar lengths, area fills over min-max axes), some correlations ship without visible n, or the hover/tap readouts are dead on a class of charts.
rubric_anchors.F: Truncated axes or area lies presented as trends, correlations framed causally or shipped with no n at all, fabricated confidence bands, or n=4 data drawn as a confident trend line with no caveat.
rubric_anchors.extension_note: Extension (not redefinition): 'contradictory encodings' includes the same series rendered with two different y-domains on two doors so the caption verdict flips, and a served probability whose numerator is entirely censored observations shorter than its own horizon — a fabricated interval by another name. Also: a literal n in a caption that disagrees with the n the payload computed counts as an F-class 'no n' for that surface, since the reader is given the wrong one.

dataviz.trend_note: B+ (2026-07-28, partial) → B: the machinery that earned the B+ (refusals, real-interval-only bands, n on correlations, keyboard readouts) is intact and live, but a from-scratch sweep found one fabricated public probability (47% odds-of-day-30 whose survivors are 100% censored 1–7-day stubs, captioned with a stale 'n=2'), a builder-level date misalignment in dualLineChart, and the results door flattening the weight slope with the very goal-in-domain rule the body hero forbids — three contradictory encodings the A anchor says must be zero.

rubric_anchors.A: Every public claim is correlative and carries a real, resolvable citation; every protocol lever states the data it targets and the hypothesis that spawned it; every pre-registered bet is either graded or explicitly voided ON THE RECORD across resets; thresholds derive from personal variance or are labelled population constants; every 'how it holds up' surface is either live or honestly retired.
rubric_anchors.C: The methodology pages state the right posture (correlative-only, pre-registration, calibration) but spot-checks find fabricated-looking citations, pre-registered bets that silently vanish at reset, or dead credibility surfaces a skeptic can trip on.
rubric_anchors.F: Causal claims stated as fact, invented or search-URL citations presented as studies, calibration numbers that misrepresent the actual record, or magic-number thresholds presented as personalized.
rubric_anchors.extension_note: EXTENSION (not a redefinition): A additionally requires (1) that an aggregate calibration label never claims a property (skilled, well-calibrated) that no constituent stratum has — pooled Brier skill against a pooled base rate is not skill; (2) that the served season ledger is a labelled mirror of the sealed artifact — every row is either in the seal or visibly marked unsealed; (3) that provenance dates on bets are event times (freeze instant, void instant), never lifecycle constants (genesis).

qs.trend_note: C+ (2026-07-28) → B: the C-anchor failures are gone — 55/55 citations resolve to the claimed papers, cycle 14/15 seals hash-verify live, and every reset's open bets are voided on the record — but the row is held below A- by a pooled career card that reads 'well-calibrated/reliable/skilled' while both strata are unskilled, and by a pre-start window in which Day-0 coach emissions were stamped as cycle-16 season bets that no surface can distinguish from the sealed 14.

Across the 8 COACH#*_coach partitions, 50 rows whose claim matches /approximately|around N|will be N|will read N|will register|sits at/ carry type=directional (49 pending incl. tombstoned, 1 confirmed); the confirmed row's outcome_notes: '{"actual_value": 0.0947…, "reason": "recovery_score trend=up (slope=0.0947), predicted=up"}'. Mechanism: coach_state_updater.py:1146-1149 `direction = _infer_direction(pred.get('direction'), claim)` → prediction_emission.py:38-51 build_prediction_eval_spec has only directional|qualitative; measurable_metrics.py infer_direction prefers the LLM extractor's `direction` field (the claim text has no DIR_UP_WORDS), so the LLM's guess becomes the graded proposition; coach_prediction_evaluator.py:728-795 scores slope sign only. findings_confirmed.verifier_reason: DDB sweep across the 8 COACH#*_coach partitions (finder's regex, evaluation.type=directional): 49 rows — 46 tombstoned pending, 2 live cycle-16 pending, 1 confirmed. The confirmed row: COACH#explorer_coach 2026-08-17 'Recovery score tomorrow will be around 50%', evaluation {condition:up, metric:recovery_score, evaluation_window_days:14}, outcome_notes 'recovery_score trend=up (slope=0.0947), predicted=up' — a one-day level claim graded as a 14-day trend, in the lifetime 8/37. Code reproduces: prediction_emission.py:38-51 build_prediction_eval_spec has only directional|qualitative; coach_state_updater.py:1146 direction = _infer_direction(pred.get('direction'), claim). Root cause is HALF wrong: the finder says the LLM extractor's guess is the source because the claim has no DIR_UP_WORDS; in fact infer_direction(None, 'Recovery score tomorrow will be around 50%') -> 'up' and infer_direction(None, 'Recovery score will be 30%') -> 'up' from text alone: DIR_UP_WORDS contains 'recover', which substring-matches the METRIC NAME 'Recovery' (measurable_metrics.py:215 `any(w in c for w in DIR_UP_WORDS)`). Controls: 'Recovery score will drop to 30%' -> None (ambiguous), 'HRV will be around 45 ms' -> None, 'Sleep score will be approximately 70' -> None — so for non-recovery metrics the extractor path the finder named applies. findings_confirmed.corrected_root_cause: Two feeders into one missing type: (1) deterministic — 'recover' in DIR_UP_WORDS substring-matches the metric name 'recovery', so every recovery_score claim without a down-word is emitted condition='up' regardless of content (the decided 08-17 row and the live 'approximately 53.5%' bet both took this path); (2) for other metrics, the LLM extractor's direction is accepted. Both land in build_prediction_eval_spec, which has no point/level type, so a level claim becomes a directional EWMA spec. Fix: word-boundary/metric-name-excluded matching in infer_direction + a point/observation class for numeric-level claims; annotate the 08-17 verdict on the record.

narrative.title: Narrative editor

rubric_anchors.A: Every live narrative surface tells one coherent cycle-6 story — reset seams are invisible to a binge reader, restored prequels are internally reconciled, each coach is distinguishable blind (and the voice-fidelity scoreboard has evidence), and no page contradicts another page's account of the same week.
rubric_anchors.C: Page-by-page prose is competent but cross-surface continuity breaks survive a reset — stale prior-cycle narratives render on live doors, restored posts contradict each other on plan facts, or coach attributions add no voice — so an attentive reader catches the machinery mis-telling the story.
rubric_anchors.F: Personas are interchangeable or the narrator voice is absent, wiped-cycle narratives dominate live pages as if current, or narrative copy contradicts the platform's own data (hype over honesty, unearned glow).
rubric_anchors.extension_note: Prior extension (2026-08-09, kept verbatim): an A additionally requires that one absence is one story — every surface narrating the same missing data agrees on its duration and cause, states n beside any rate, and never grades a zero-observation set. EXTENDED 2026-09-04 (surface grew — the reset is now a weekly-cadence event with scheduled writers running between reset and Day 1): an A additionally requires that the story the reset tells at reset time is STILL the story every scheduled writer tells at the first cron after it — a surface the reset honestly emptied may not be re-populated by any job that derives 'publishable' from something other than the phase registry.

narrative.trend_note: B+ (2026-08-16) → C+: the static Saturday re-anchor and the prologue reconciliation are genuinely A-grade work, but a daily writer re-published the sealed cycle's Week 1 onto the home page and the story door on the eve of Day 1 — the C anchor's 'stale prior-cycle narratives render on live doors' met literally — and it armed a Day-1 recap the guard cannot see.

rubric_anchors.A: Live public JSON exposes zero chronological age / birth year / genome identifiers / vice-substance names (verified by curl+grep, not docs); sensitive S3 prefixes (raw/config/uploads/dashboard) return 403/404 publicly; no live secret or PII in tracked repo files or recent history; the MCP OAuth consent+PKCE gate and DDB-backed per-IP rate limits are provably enforced with no spoofable trust boundary; every Lambda has its own least-privilege role with Resource:* only on actions that cannot be resource-scoped.
rubric_anchors.C: Privacy absolutes hold on the sampled live endpoints but one enforcement boundary is bypassable (e.g. spoofable client-IP so rate limits don't actually bind) or a known-inversion residual is unmitigated, OR an over-broad IAM wildcard / publicly readable sensitive prefix exists without a compensating control.
rubric_anchors.F: Any live public endpoint returns chronological age, a genome identifier, or a named vice/substance; a live credential is committed to the repo; /token or /authorize mints a bearer without consent; or raw health data is publicly fetchable.
rubric_anchors.extension_note: EXTENSION (not a redefinition): the A anchor's 'no PII in tracked repo files' is extended to 'no THIRD-PARTY PII (reader-supplied email/ip_hash) written into an anonymously-readable S3 prefix', because the platform now takes reader input on two public doors and the ADR-046 generated/ prefix is world-readable by bucket policy. A prefix that is public BY DESIGN (generated/*) counts as a 'publicly readable sensitive prefix' the moment a reader-input door writes PII into it.

a11y.title: Accessibility specialist

rubric_anchors.A: WCAG AA holds on every live page in BOTH themes (verified by an automated token-contrast check, not hand-written comments); every interactive widget is keyboard-operable with visible focus; data charts are named to AT; reduced-motion is honored; tap targets meet the 44px floor site-wide with a gating audit.
rubric_anchors.C: Landmarks/headings/skip links are mostly right and most widgets are keyboard-reachable, but multiple AA contrast failures exist in at least one theme, some custom widgets (charts, tabs, popovers) are mouse-only or unnamed to screen readers, and there is no regression guard so fixes decay.
rubric_anchors.F: Div-soup interactive UI (no focus styles, no keyboard path), data charts silent to screen readers, contrast failures on body text, no skip links, animation ignores prefers-reduced-motion.
rubric_anchors.extension_note: EXTENSION (not a redefinition): 'verified by an automated token-contrast check' is read to include COMPOSITED text (opacity/color-mix over a surface) and every palette used as text (pillar/coach accents), because the two live AA classes found this run are invisible to a full-opacity token pair check by construction. 'a gating audit' is read to require that the debt ledger the gate compares against is CURRENT: a baselined rule the page no longer exhibits is a disarmed gate, not a guard. 'the 44px floor' is measured against WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8's 24x24 minimum as the hard floor, with 44 as the target — a rule that passes a 2x44 hit box is not a floor.

a11y.trend_note: A- (2026-07-28) → B+: the machinery is as strong as in July (four ledgers now, light and mobile axes added, tap gate non-vacuous), but the July grade was conditional on the ledger shrink landing and staying current — instead the ledger has re-accreted 11 stale keys, the shrink signal still has no consumer (July path-to-A step 4 never landed), the two AA classes on the flagship data pages (opacity-recede text, pillar text in light) were fixed only as instances (#1989, #2919/#3057) while the class survives at ~230 nodes, and no open issue tracks any accessibility debt at all.

findings_refuted.summary: The subscribe email field suppresses the focus ring and signals focus only by recolouring a 1px hairline border — the one form control on the reader-facing write path has the weakest focus indicator on the site.
findings_refuted.evidence: site/assets/css/subscribe.css:48 `.sub-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--ember); }`; the border is `--border-hair: 1px solid var(--rule)` (tokens.css:290) where --rule is rgba(236,227,210,0.12) dark / rgba(34,30,23,0.13) light — so the focus change is a 1px stroke going from a ~12% hairline to ember. The `.sub-input:focus` (0,2,0) selector outranks the site's element-level :focus-visible rules (tokens.css: 14 focus-visible rules, e.g. story.css:266 `.wave a.bar:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ember); outline-offset: 2px; }`), so the shared 2px ring never applies here. WCAG 2.4.7 (AA) is arguably met by the colour change; 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (2px-equivalent area, 3:1 change) is not, and it is the only control on the site styled this way (grep 'outline:\s*(none|0)' site/assets/css → this one hit).
findings_refuted.class: focus indicator replaced by a sub-threshold colour change on a form control
findings_refuted.regression_guard: Replace with `.sub-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ember); outline-offset: 2px; }` and extend tests/test_site_a11y_landmarks.py (or a new static CSS test) to assert no `outline: none|0` in site/assets/css without a sibling :focus-visible outline rule.
findings_refuted.blast_radius: /subscribe/ and the inline subscribe cards (subscribe.css is shared); keyboard users only.
findings_refuted.verifier_reason: The finder missed the override 41 lines below the cited rule in the SAME file: site/assets/css/subscribe.css:89 `.sub-btn:focus-visible, .sub-input:focus-visible, .doors a:focus-visible, .theme-toggle:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ember); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: var(--radius-xs); }` — specificity (0,2,0) equals `.sub-input:focus` at line 48 and it is later in the cascade, so it wins whenever :focus-visible matches (which browsers apply to text inputs on every focus). Live proof (Playwright, https://averagejoematt.com/subscribe/, 2 `.sub-input` elements, first focused): dark → {active: True, fv: True, outlineStyle: 'solid', outlineWidth: '2px', outlineColor: 'rgb(221, 122, 55)', outlineOffset: '2px'}; light → outline solid 2px rgb(163, 78, 19) offset 2px. The shared 2px ember ring DOES apply; the claim 'the shared 2px ring never applies here' and 'the only control on the site styled this way' are both false. The `outline: none` at :48 only suppresses the UA default ring for the (theoretical) :focus-not-:focus-visible case, which for a text input does not occur in practice. Not a defect.
findings_refuted.corrected_root_cause: No defect — a cascade misread; the later equal-specificity :focus-visible rule restores the site's 2px ring.

reader.title: First-time reader (persona, on LIVE pages)

rubric_anchors.A: A stranger from Reddit gets what/who/why in one screen on every door, every platform term is glossed inline where it first appears, every visible number is self-consistent and date-scoped, and a 4-day-old experiment reads as deliberately young rather than empty or broken.
rubric_anchors.C: The pages render and the premise is findable, but unexplained jargon, contradictory or stale numbers, or broken-looking text force the reader to do reconciliation work before they can trust the site.
rubric_anchors.F: A first-time reader cannot tell what the site is or whether it is alive — blank regions, raw template bindings, dead data, or a story surface that looks abandoned.
rubric_anchors.extension_note: EXTENSION (surface moved to Day 0, wording unchanged): the A-clause 'a 4-day-old experiment reads as deliberately young' is read to cover a Day-0 countdown — the premiere must read as a deliberate premiere — and 'every visible number is self-consistent and date-scoped' is read to include a prior cycle's writing: it may be reachable only when it is labeled as the prior cycle's, never as 'Week 1' / 'latest' of the cycle that has not started. No redefinition.

observability.title: Observability lead

rubric_anchors.A: Every alarm state is honest (red = a real, actionable condition; nothing permanently red or structurally unclearable), every watchdog's producer is verified actually emitting (not just designed to), and the remediation/drift loop demonstrably closes or explicitly hands off every signal it sees — all within the $85 ceiling, urgent-vs-digest split intact, solo operator paged for what matters and only that.
rubric_anchors.C: The alarm inventory is well-designed on paper but one or more watchdog producers are dead (IAM/emission failures swallowed as warnings), red alarms sit unactioned for a week-plus, or the self-healing loop completes triage only intermittently while reporting green — governance expressed but not achieved.
rubric_anchors.F: Alarms missing or routed to nowhere (no live SNS subscription), DLQ pileup or a dead ingestion source discoverable only by manual audit, budget hard-stop silent, log groups unbounded — the operator learns about failures from the website being wrong.
rubric_anchors.extension_note: EXTENSION (not a redefinition): the A clause 'the loop explicitly hands off every signal' is read to require that a hand-off be about the CURRENT state and have a terminal condition — a needs-human line that repeats verbatim every run about a state that a later deploy already replaced, or that the producer can never satisfy by construction, is not a hand-off; it is noise the operator learns to skip. Likewise 'every alarm state is honest' extends to the acknowledgement layers on top of the alarm (docs/alarm_citations.json, remediation-log/ack_ledger.json): a green citation gate over a citation written for a PREVIOUS episode is a dishonest layer on an honest alarm. Ceiling figure in the A anchor is historical ($85); the platform's stated ceiling is now $215/$252 (ADR-133) and the grade uses that.

observability.trend_note: A- → B+: the alarm estate itself is healthier than at the 08-16 delta (heartbeat pairs complete and live, composites verified routing, all reds true positives, retention bounded), but a from-scratch baseline found a QA watchdog that has never produced its measurement behind a chronic flag (OBS-1), an acknowledgement layer that passes green over a citation written for a previous episode while the agent stores a false 'resolved' (OBS-2), and a self-healing hand-off that repeats an unfillable cadence gap and a superseded drift record every run (OBS-3) — the C-anchor's 'IAM failure swallowed as a warning' and 'reporting green' clauses, each in one specimen.

cost.title: Cost engineer

rubric_anchors.A: The ADR-063/133 ceiling is enforced at the bedrock_client chokepoint with the ADR-125 audience-ordered ladder, the projection math has no double-count or de-escalation traps, every public and operator-facing cost number (ceiling, monthly total, tier labels) matches the live governor state per ADR-104, and per-feature AI cost is visible on a live public receipt.
rubric_anchors.C: A hard stop exists somewhere but the tier labels, public cost numbers, and the actual degradation ladder disagree with each other; or the projection has a known over/under-count failure mode; or the operator cannot attribute AI spend per feature.
rubric_anchors.F: No near-real-time enforcement (AWS Budgets alone with its 24-48h Bedrock lag), reader traffic can spend unbounded through the public AI endpoints, or the public cost claims are fabricated rather than derived from metering.
rubric_anchors.extension_note: EXTENSION (not a redefinition): 'matches the live governor state' now also requires that a published projection state its SCOPE when the governor extrapolates a subset of spend (#2892 projects prod-cron+remediation only). A correctly derived subset presented to readers as 'projected month-end' is a C-anchor disagreement between public number and governor state, not an A. Second extension: a ceiling that floats on a traffic threshold is only 'enforced' if the threshold sits outside the baseline's own variance (ADR-105 thresholds-from-variance applies to the ceiling's inputs, not just to alarms).

cost.trend_note: B+ (2026-07-28) → B+: the enforcement core measurably improved (base derived from a measured steady state per #2801, the #2892 class split, per-feature dollar ledger #3374, drift reconciled to ≈1.00) but two honesty gaps opened or went unnoticed since — the public projection is an unlabeled subset that AWS's own forecast contradicts 2x, and the surge threshold has been flipping the ceiling on weekly noise since July — and the per-feature kill switch (#3373) is still absent, so the area holds its grade rather than moving to A-.

rubric_anchors.A: Live DynamoDB items, docs/SCHEMA.md, and the phase-taxonomy registry are mutually consistent under spot-sampling; exactly the 2 sanctioned GSIs (ADR-097) exist; the reset machinery is provably total AND idempotent (a double reset preserves each record's original cycle provenance); raw-S3 layouts match their source_registry raw_layout facets including filename scheme.
rubric_anchors.C: The schema doc is mostly accurate and GSI count holds, but the reset/provenance machinery drifts from its stated contract in live data (wrong cycle stamps, claimed write-time stamping absent), or new pk families can silently escape the taxonomy's totality guarantee.
rubric_anchors.F: Undocumented GSIs or partitions in live; float writes crashing or silently failing DDB persistence; tombstoned records from a prior cycle leaking into current-cycle reads; or archive records destroyed/overwritten with no way to reconstruct provenance.
rubric_anchors.extension_note: Extended, not redefined: (1) 'total' is read against the LIVE pk-family census, not only SOURCE_CLASS — a non-SOURCE family (COACH#<name>) that classify() calls EXPERIMENT_SCOPED but no wipe list visits is a totality escape; (2) 'provenance' includes agreement between a row's cycle stamp and closing_cycle_for_genesis(genesis-in-tombstoned_reason) under an in-place re-anchor; (3) the F 'float write' clause covers a crash that loses a record whose side effect (a sent email, Bedrock spend) already happened; (4) 'tombstoned records leaking' includes WRITER-side resurrection (a status-only selector republishing a tombstoned row), not only reader-side filters.

The registry function is used only by deploy/reconcile_prereg_voids.py (retrospective backfill), while restart_pipeline.py:840-856 reads the closing cycle from SSM by design (ADR-077) — two sources with different jobs, not a defect. DID NOT: run the full pytest suite or any pytest; inspect the 40 MCP modules' write paths for Decimal hygiene; verify each of the ~10 newest-first scoped readers' guards individually (only counted cycle_read_floor adopters); compare SCHEMA.md field tables to live attributes beyond family presence; check raw leaves outside 2026-09 or the whoop/health_auto_export sub-layout months; sample log groups beyond the 50 matched by name (54 Lambdas unsampled for float crashes); read PERSONA#/ENSEMBLE# tombstone contents; independently verify the tagger's '50 rows re-phased' or the 314 count (my census cannot distinguish the 09-03 and 09-04 passes on rows already tombstoned earlier); reconcile my 99-family grouping with the pipeline's '98 pk families' (different grouping — not claimed as a delta); examine GSI2's 6 rows; examine DIL-027 replication or backups. The writer inventory (DA-5) is a static grep/awk heuristic (window ±45 lines around put_item/update_item, then module-level mention) — it over-approximates module mentions and can miss writers that build pks in helpers; the four co-owned records named were each confirmed by reading the write sites.
data-architect.process_verdict: Three layers should have caught these before a review did. (1) The reset's own verify (restart_verify / the #3390 Day-1 runlist) has no post-reset DATA census: it renders pages and checks alarms but never asserts 'no EXPERIMENT_SCOPED row dated < genesis without phase=pilot', 'no CROSS_PHASE row tombstoned', 'every classify()==EXPERIMENT_SCOPED pk family is in the wipe's covered set', or 'cycle stamps agree with closing_cycle_for_genesis' — add these as a step-N census gate (the same scan step-0 already runs) and make the 48h auto-publish sweep's negative control part of it. (2) The /new-machinery contract primitive was applied producer→consumer (8 pairs) but never writer↔writer, so #3443's fix guarded one instance while the class stayed open (habit_scores' duplicated writer, chronicle's status-vs-tombstone) — extend the registry with a CoOwned entry type and require it whenever a second module gains a put/update on an existing key. (3) Decimal hygiene has no derivation guard at all (no AST gate, no dead-man on 'attempting' ledger rows), so a float crash after an email send was invisible for 5 days until a review's Logs Insights query — add the AST gate to CI's lint job and the ledger dead-man to nightly qa-smoke. The through-line matches Session U's: instruments (assert_registry_coverage, the stamp audit, the recap day-guard, the sweep's 10-day 'pre-genesis leftover' guard) that enumerate from a hand-typed list or floor their comparand to the passing value, and therefore cannot fail on the case they were written for.
verifier_notes: Three of five findings refuted on a false premise (DA-3's 'correct stamp is 15', DA-4's floor-as-hole, DA-5's 'put twice daily' + phantom second writer), one is an already-filed issue (#3485), and DA-2 drops to P3 (13 inert dedupe rows). What survives is DA-1 — and it is larger than filed: coach-nudge has never persisted a single nudge since #1382 shipped (0 NUDGE# rows, 4/4 ledger rows 'attempting', 3/3 in-retention runs dead on the same float after the email left), a Decimal-hygiene miss at one write site ordered after an irreversible side effect, undetected because nothing dead-mans the ledger — plus the S2(ii) provenance contradiction on RELATIONSHIP#state (P4). Against the anchors, the data layer's primitives are largely holding (tombstones honoured by readers, wipe coverage assertion works for the coach roster, computed_metrics co-ownership guarded since #3457); the confirmed gaps are one unguarded write site and one prefix-rule-vs-hand-list enumeration gap. That supports the prior B+ rather than a downgrade to B. Coverage: I did not re-derive the seed's '98/98 classification' or '314/45' ledger figures, did not audit the other write sites for float coercion beyond coach-nudge (the finder's 50-log-group Insights sweep was not re-run), did not run any pytest, and did not examine the six unstamped INSIGHT#2026-09-03 rows referenced as DA-7 (not in this batch). Read-only throughout: no invocations, no writes, no gh writes; scan was a projected, filtered read of 42,598 items.

All five batch-2 findings survive with corrections (DA-10 loses its PULSE claim; DA-8's cited accessor name is wrong and its scope is larger; DA-7's class is #1814 not #2113). Seed S1 is confirmed and EXTENDED: the phantom Friday anchor is on a public surface — /api/calibration voided.by_reset['2026-09-05'] = 17 on Day 0, the 17 not being on the do-not-refile list (the 45 are); that is the most material item here and lifts S1 to P2. Seed S2 is half wrong (habit_scores fallback-only; engagement_state single-writer). Everything else in this batch is P3 provenance/doc drift on machinery the registry already classifies correctly at read/wipe time, so B holds: nothing serves pilot content as current, but write-time provenance is decided per partition by three writers while the registry rules per row, and no census assertion closes the inverse direction. Coverage: I did not re-run the finder's ddb_drill (its /tmp/x.json is gone) so the '99 families' and cross_experiment bucket counts are taken from targeted queries, not a full scan; I did not enumerate the '~10 newest-first readers' in DA-7; no Lambda invoked, no writes, no full pytest. Tree at verification: HEAD 17143485c (one commit past the brief's a16d4368a), only .claude/settings.local.json dirty.

integrations.title: Integrations engineer

rubric_anchors.A: Every source's declared cadence/threshold matches its live EventBridge rule with a written derivation (the #471 Todoist standard); the public board and the operator checker tell the same cross-reset-honest story (real last_update + 'dark N days'); a dead OAuth token pages within ~one cadence via alarms that are green because they work, not because they can't fire; dead sources are disclosed everywhere they surface — all with no machinery beyond the one canonical registry.
rubric_anchors.C: Cadences and thresholds are mostly honest, but at least one public surface omits or misstates staleness (e.g. a real lapse rendered as 'no data' with no duration), or a dead source appears live on a reader-facing surface, or token death is only noticed by a daily human glance rather than an alarm.
rubric_anchors.F: Registry facets contradict the live rules (thresholds impossible for the cadence), staleness is silently hidden or fabricated on the public board, dead sources are presented as flowing, and there is no alarm path for a dead token.
rubric_anchors.extension_note: EXTENSION (not a redefinition): the A bar's 'green because they work' clause now explicitly covers the checker's OWN sub-instruments (episode dedup, absence markers, sentinel writes) — a write the role cannot perform, logged as 'non-fatal' at ERROR every run, is a dead instrument, and a consumer that claims to derive from the registry must actually read the facet it derives from (behavioral, expected_days), not a hand-rolled proxy.

integrations.trend_note: A- → B+: cadences, thresholds, the public board, token-death paging and webhook dedup all still meet the A anchor, but this baseline found a checker sub-instrument (the #1480 episode dedup) that has been IAM-denied on every run for 49 days with the denial logged 'non-fatal' and invisible to every alarm, plus two guard-the-set gaps (the seed's classifier and the #2643 marker on one of four daily sources) — the platform's recurring 'instruments unable to fail' class, on the ingestion row this time.

rubric_anchors.A: Every load-bearing claim an agent reads in its first 5 minutes (CLAUDE.md, CONVENTIONS, the /deploy skill) is either machine-synced or provably current; all deploy paths verifiably stage through one bundle; the fast deploy-critical lane runs green offline in seconds; incident classes are encoded in gates/agents rather than relying on agent memory; drift gates cover process/ownership/date facts, not just counts.
rubric_anchors.C: The one-bundle rule and CI gates exist and mostly work, but agent-facing docs carry multiple contradictions an agent must resolve by reading source (stale ship paths, wrong stack owners, dead command signatures), the doc-sync gates cover only what they were hand-taught, and a fresh agent's first deploy requires tribal knowledge from memory topics to avoid a known incident class.
rubric_anchors.F: Deploy paths diverge (some functions ship partial bundles), CLAUDE.md commands fail or silently do the wrong thing, CI pins drift from local tooling so local-green != CI-green, and the handover/memory system has rotted into an unindexed pile — a fresh agent's first change is more likely to regress production than to land.
rubric_anchors.extension_note: EXTENSION (not a redefinition): 'incident classes are encoded in gates' is read to include the instruments that READ CI — check_main_green.py / check_ci_warnings.py / wait_pr_green.sh. An A requires that main's own green-reader cannot classify a run carrying a real failing job as 'no signal', and that every local check claiming to mirror a CI job DERIVES its step set from the workflow file (the #3477/#3479 class, generalized) rather than restating a subset.

devex.trend_note: A- → B+: the deploy plane (one bundle, single-source pins, hook parity) is still A-grade and S2 was fixed at the root, but the run-history read shows main's own green-readers (check_main_green/check_ci_warnings) carry a premise falsified by the 2026-08-02 concurrency redesign, Docs CI cancels ~40% of its own main verdicts by config, and the #3477 'subset of a gate' class was encoded for the reset only — the wrap battery and the merge watch still restate what they claim to mirror, which is the A-anchor's 'incident classes encoded in gates rather than agent memory' failing in the exact week the class was named.

findings_confirmed.summary: check_main_green.py and check_ci_warnings.py skip every `cancelled` CI/CD run as 'a superseded push with no signal' — but since the 2026-08-02 per-run workflow group nothing supersedes a CI/CD run; a `cancelled` rollup on main is now minted by the deploy job's `ci-cd-deploy-<ref>` concurrency group cancelling the older WAITING Deploy when the next run's Deploy queues (GitHub's one-pending-slot rule), while `test / Unit Tests` in that same run FAILED. Two live specimens on 2026-09-04 carried a real coverage-gate failure that both instruments discard.
findings_confirmed.evidence: gh run view 33843742114 --json jobs → `failure  test / Unit Tests … Test coverage gate (regression floor, ADR-080)`, `cancelled  Deploy 06:29:10→06:33:51` with ZERO steps and `gh api …/runs/33843742114/approvals` → empty (no rejection record); same shape in 33843452894 (Unit Tests failure, Deploy cancelled 06:24:21→06:29:11). The Deploy cancellation instants (06:29:11, 06:33:51) equal the NEXT run's Deploy start (33843742114 Deploy started 06:29:10; 33844077590 followed). Run rollups: `gh run list --workflow CI/CD --branch main` → `33843742114 cancelled`, `33843452894 cancelled`. scripts/check_main_green.py:196 'Cancelled runs are superseded pushes, not verdicts; skip' and :204 `if r.get("conclusion") == "cancelled": continue`; scripts/check_ci_warnings.py latest_green_main_info() skips `conclusion == "cancelled"`. .github/workflows/ci-cd.yml:129 `group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.run_id }}` (per-run, never superseded) and :861-862 `group: ci-cd-deploy-${{ github.ref }} / cancel-in-progress: false`. docs/CONVENTIONS.md §4 states 'with cancel-in-progress: false that only happens on a manual cancel' — false.

findings_confirmed.blast_radius: Every /wrap main-green gate and every CI-warning triage since 2026-08-02 can read a real Unit Tests red as 'nothing to decode' whenever two merges land within one deploy-lease window — which is every merge-train session; #3422's janitor makes the pending-slot cancel MORE frequent, not less.
findings_confirmed.verifier_reason: Reproduced end to end. `gh run view 33843742114 --json jobs` → `failure test / Unit Tests 06:22:01→06:50:37`, `cancelled Deploy 06:29:10→06:33:51`; `…/runs/33843742114/approvals` → `[]`. Adjacent runs prove the mechanism: 33843452894 Deploy cancelled 06:29:11 == 33843742114 Deploy started 06:29:10; 33843742114 Deploy cancelled 06:33:51 == 33844077590 Deploy started 06:33:51 (group `ci-cd-deploy-${{ github.ref }}`, ci-cd.yml:861-862; workflow group is per-run at :129 since commit 908417617 / #2009, 2026-08-01 — not 08-02, immaterial). Pure-function reproduction of the reader with a fixture [cancelled@HEAD, success@OLD]: `latest_completed_run → success@OLDSHA`, `head_coverage → pending`, `head_coverage_ok → True`, `latest_main_conclusion → ('success','OLDSHA')` — so a real Unit Tests red at HEAD reads as a green older sha plus a 'normal post-merge pending'. `check_ci_warnings.py:88` has the identical skip. `docs/CONVENTIONS.md:163` still says cancellation 'only happens on a manual cancel' — false per the two specimens. Extra root-cause detail the finder missed: the deploy job `needs: [reconcile, plan]` (NOT the Unit Tests job), which is why Deploy can enter the group, be pending-slot-cancelled, and stamp the rollup `cancelled` ~17 min BEFORE Unit Tests reports failure. Not a duplicate: `gh issue list --search cancelled/rollup` returns only the auto-filed wedge issues and #1901 (stranded approval, closed); HANDOVER_LATEST.md:170 and the memory note record it as a 'open the steps' lesson, not a gate.
findings_confirmed.corrected_root_cause: Two skips read the run ROLLUP (`conclusion == cancelled`) as 'superseded push'; since #2009 (2026-08-01) the only thing that cancels a main CI/CD run is the deploy job's `ci-cd-deploy-<ref>` group evicting the older pending Deploy when the next run's Deploy queues, and Deploy does not `needs` the Unit Tests job, so the rollup goes `cancelled` while a real test failure is still in flight. `head_coverage()` then classifies the cancelled HEAD run as `pending` (an OK state), so the wrap gate stays green on the previous sha.

findings_confirmed.regression_guard: tests/test_docs_ci_owns_doc_gates.py: parse docs-ci.yml and assert the concurrency group includes `${{ github.sha }}` (or cancel-in-progress is `${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}`) so a push to main can never cancel another push's run; keep cancel-in-progress for PR refs only. findings_confirmed.blast_radius: Every merge that adds a test (most feature PRs) plus any concurrent docs push; the human commit's Docs CI verdict is lost on ~40% of main pushes, so a genuine dead link/tombstone/model drift introduced by the human commit is attributed to nothing until a later push happens to re-run clean or red.
findings_confirmed.verifier_reason: Evidence reproduces: 16 of the last 40 Docs CI runs on main are `cancelled` (finder said 17 — the window moved by one); run 33935174277 (17143485) job `cancelled Wiki drift gates` with step `failure Literal-drift gate (sync_doc_metadata --check)` and all 11 other gates success, and ALL 16 steps including 'Complete job' finished before the cancel stamp; bot run 33935216861 (9709ac65) success created 48 s later; docs-ci.yml:152-156 and v4-gate.yml:42-46 carry `cancel-in-progress: true` on group `<workflow>-<ref>`. #1453's rationale was Pro-plan minute metering while the repo was PRIVATE (it went public 2026-07-20), so the rent argument is dead. BUT the severity premise is overstated: on a linear main the superseding run re-executes all 12 gates on a SUPERSET tree, so the tree's verdict is not lost — the bot's green 48 s later IS the honest verdict for main; what is lost is per-commit attribution and rollup legibility (a job that ran to completion with one red is stamped `cancelled`). No instrument reads Docs CI rollups: docs-ci.yml has one job and no `if: failure()` notify job; deploy/sentinel_github.py only detects zero-run heads (no `conclusion` read); check_main_green reads CI/CD only. So this is a legibility/attribution defect with a cheap fix (sha in the group for push events), not a lost-verdict defect. Not filed as an issue; HANDOVER_LATEST.md:162 records it as a lesson only.
findings_confirmed.corrected_root_cause: cancel-in-progress on a push-to-main group turns a completed-and-failed job into a `cancelled` rollup whenever the reconcile bot (or any push) lands within ~90 s; the loss is attribution and rollup honesty, not tree verification — the superseding run verifies a superset tree. Rent justification for the cancel (#1453 CI minutes) no longer applies on a public repo.

findings_confirmed.summary: check_doc_index.py's engine-doc source-drift gate dates each declared source by `git log -1 --format=%cs` — committed dates only — so an UNCOMMITTED rewrite of a source (config/character_sheet.json, which the reset regenerates) is invisible; deploy/restart_verify_gates.py runs this gate BEFORE the reset commit and therefore runs a gate that structurally cannot see the artifacts the reset just wrote. Its own module docstring and tests/test_restart_verify_gates_3477.py then claim the sweep is 'read-only by contract', asserting only that no argv contains '--apply' — while the derived list includes `skill_lint.py --self-test`, which docs-ci.yml itself documents as mutating a tracked file in place.

Derived list (python3 -c … docs_ci_gate_commands()) includes `python3 scripts/skill_lint.py --self-test`; docs-ci.yml:253-257 'Kept out of pytest because it mutates a tracked file in place'. tests/test_restart_verify_gates_3477.py:48-52 `assert "--apply" not in cmd`; :28-37 the 'independently re-derived' parity function is the byte-identical regex, so it agrees with the parser by construction.

findings_confirmed.regression_guard: check_doc_index: union `git status --porcelain` paths with date=today before comparing to the Verified stamp (mutation test: dirty a declared source, assert strict red). restart_verify_gates test: run the sweep on a fixture tree and assert `git status --porcelain` is byte-identical before/after; have the parity test parse docs-ci.yml with PyYAML and assert every step whose `run` contains 'python3' is derived (so a future `run: |` gate cannot go dark).
findings_confirmed.blast_radius: Every reset: the CHARACTER.md re-verify the sweep's own failure text tells the operator to do by hand is exactly the drift this gate could catch pre-commit if it read the tree.
findings_confirmed.verifier_reason: Narrowed to one of its three legs. Leg 1 (history-keyed gate run pre-commit) reproduces: scripts/check_doc_index.py:164 `['git','log','-1','--format=%cs','--',rel_path]`, `grep -c 'porcelain\|diff --name'` = 0; deploy/restart_pipeline.py:735 runs restart_verify_gates LAST and the pipeline never commits (git commit is left to the operator, :1184); config/character_sheet.json is git-tracked and rewritten by the reset; the sweep's own failure text (:128) tells the operator to re-verify CHARACTER.md by hand. BUT the platform already knows: handovers/HANDOVER_LATEST.md:302-308 ('The engine-doc gate cannot be caught pre-commit… structurally invisible to the #3477 sweep') and the CHARACTER.md Verified stamp itself ('NOTE for the next reset: this gate compares COMMIT dates, so it cannot fire until the config is committed'). No issue was filed, so the finding is new to the backlog, not new knowledge. Leg 2 (skill_lint --self-test makes the sweep a writer) is REFUTED: scripts/skill_lint.py:487-510 and :522-540 take an on-disk tempfile backup and restore in `finally`; the tree is byte-identical on any normal exit — the 'read-only' claim holds by effect, only the TEST phrases it as `'--apply' not in cmd`. findings_confirmed.summary: scheduled_workflow_registry.py's deploy-wedge-watch row sets grace 8h on a 2026-08-26 measurement ('20-209 min … median ~47 min … 8h is ~2.3x the worst observed gap'); re-measured n=60 scheduled runs 08-26→09-04 the gaps are median 211 min, p90 419, max 729 min (12.1h) — above the 8.25h deadline (0.25h cadence + 8h grace). The dead-man's basis is a founding-week snapshot, not an invariant (the #3447 class), so the push-triggered cron-freshness check will rule this healthy workflow `late` on an ordinary GitHub delay and train the reader to ignore the one instrument built to say 'the scheduler stopped'.
findings_confirmed.evidence: scripts/scheduled_workflow_registry.py:117-124 `"grace_hours": 8.0, "basis": "declared */15; MEASURED 20-209 min between the 20 newest scheduled runs (2026-08-26, median ~47 min) … 8h is ~2.3x the worst observed gap."`. Re-measurement: gh run list --workflow 'Deploy wedge watch' --limit 60 (event==schedule) → n=60, first 2026-08-26T11:02Z last 2026-09-04T23:36Z, gap min/median/p90/max = 21/211/419/729 min, 58/59 gaps > 30 min. .github/workflows/deploy-wedge-watch.yml:52-55 '15 minutes bounds the blind window below that' — the header's design assumption; cron-freshness.yml has NO schedule (push-triggered, by design #3213).
findings_confirmed.reproduction: gh run list --workflow 'Deploy wedge watch' --limit 60 --json createdAt,event --jq '.[] | select(.event=="schedule") | .createdAt' | python3 -c "import sys,datetime as d; ts=sorted(d.datetime.fromisoformat(l.strip().replace('Z','+00:00')) for l in sys.stdin if l.strip()); g=sorted((b-a).total_seconds()/60 for a,b in zip(ts,ts[1:])); print(len(ts), g[len(g)//2], g[int(len(g)*.9)], g[-1])"; sed -n 117,124p scripts/scheduled_workflow_registry.py
findings_confirmed.class: a measured threshold whose basis is a snapshot — the registry records the number and the date but nothing re-derives it (#3447's class, scheduler edition)
findings_confirmed.regression_guard: Store the basis as a derivation (window + percentile, e.g. 'max observed gap over trailing 60 scheduled runs × 1.5') that check_cron_freshness.py re-computes from the Actions API at run time, with the registry literal only as a floor; a test asserts the literal is ≥ the live max when GitHub is reachable, UNVERIFIED otherwise.
findings_confirmed.blast_radius: The one watched high-frequency row; the weekly/daily rows have 14-24h grace and are unaffected. The wedge-watch header's '15 minutes bounds the blind window' claim is the same stale assumption — that leg is the open #3422 cadence item, not refiled here.
findings_confirmed.verifier_reason: Evidence reproduces and the premise is STRONGER than filed: this is not a prediction, it already happened. My re-measure (gh run list --workflow 'Deploy wedge watch' --limit 60, all 60 event==schedule): n=60, 2026-08-26T11:43Z→2026-09-05T01:23Z, gap min/median/p90/max = 21/211/419/729 min; three gaps exceed the 8.25h deadline (557, 666, 729 min — all 08-27/28). Crossing those against all 266 cron-freshness push runs: on 2026-08-27 15:54→17:38Z SIX runs failed with `[ STALE] deploy-wedge-watch.yml newest sched run 9.0h…10.73h ago (deadline 8.25h = cadence 0.25h + grace 8.0h)` (runs 33090434263, 33094047028, 33094295090, 33094748796, 33099236425, 33099453236 — logs read), auto-filing #3237, which auto-closed 18:10Z on the next delivered cron. Session G's decode on #3237 measured n=99 (max 6.99h) and wrote the finder's exact guard as disposition item 3 ('Re-deriving grace from the measured distribution rather than from the last maximum is the durable version'), then folded it 'onto the owning epic' — none of the 8 open epics mentions wedge-watch or grace, and scripts/scheduled_workflow_registry.py:117-124 is untouched since #3229 (519f93a3b changed 0 wedge lines). Since 08-29 the max gap is 460 min (n=45) — 35 min under the deadline — so the next false red is one slow GitHub morning away. Worst age at a push: 10.73h. Registry row is prose ('basis' string), nothing re-derives it. Sev P3 stands; corrected framing: extends #3237 (closed, auto-closed on recovery with its disposition unactioned).
findings_confirmed.corrected_root_cause: The 8h grace was tuned to the founding-week max (6.99h) and breached the next day; the auto-close-on-recovery policy retired the red before the decode's fix could land, and the fold target is not findable among open epics.

growth.title: Growth PM

rubric_anchors.A: Every shareable page emits a current, data-driven OG card; the subscribe flow is double-opt-in, canary-tested, AND its conversion (attempts → confirms → list size) is visible in the weekly traffic digest; subscribers get a fixed cadence that matches the promise copy on /subscribe/; engagement hooks (predict, board-ask, votes) work on Day 1 of a fresh cycle and are discoverable from the pages newcomers land on; commercial option value (list, RSS, gear, podcast) is real and measured with zero dishonest monetization.
rubric_anchors.C: Capture and email machinery works end-to-end but the funnel is unmeasured (signups can silently die in pending state), share surfaces ship a generic or stale card, and engagement hooks exist in code but are not reachable or not functional on Day 1 of a cycle.
rubric_anchors.F: The funnel is broken or dishonest: subscribe silently fails or is single-opt-in spam, share cards present wrong/stale numbers as current, engagement endpoints 500, or monetization (undisclosed affiliates, paywalled 'proof') contradicts the proof-not-promises posture.
rubric_anchors.extension_note: EXTENSION (not a redefinition): the F clause 'share cards present wrong/stale numbers as current' is read to cover the whole share surface — /moments/index.json, /moments/share-kits/*/kit.json and the /journal/posts/week-NN/ permalinks those kits canonicalise — because a previous cycle's article served at its public URL with no notice, or a share kit that still advertises a voided cycle's Week 1, is the same defect as a stale card. Also: the C clause 'stale card' is read to include a hard-coded placeholder card on a topic page whose API serves null (og-glucose).

growth.trend_note: C+ (2026-08-02) → C+: both clauses that earned the prior C+ are genuinely closed (the kill switch is lifted with a live guard, the funnel is in the Monday digest), but the story/share surface today serves prior-cycle content as current — every reset leaves week-03/04/05 articles live because the archive step is slug-idempotent, and the resurrected cycle-15 'Week 1 — 328.1' share kit survived the #3485 repair — which is the F anchor's 'stale numbers as current' on the syndication path, while the subscriber promise ('one email a week, every Wednesday') is still false on cadence, day and count; the machinery is better, the honesty of what a newcomer can be handed is not yet.

Not filed (60 closed / 33 open / HANDOVER: no match; #733 and #353 added posts to the sitemap, neither touched fragment exclusion). WORSE than filed: the sitemap's body URL is a dead end, not just a redirect — curl -w: /body → 301 → /body/ → 404, while /body.html → 200. url_for() (:40-45) strips the .html suffix for every non-index file, emitting a URL form the CDN cannot serve; body.html and subscribe.html are the only two non-index files that survive indexable() today (all other extensionless sitemap URLs: just those two). The RSS-autodiscovery leg is the weakest part: 24 pages (story/coaching/journal/subscribe/privacy) carry the link, 66 (cockpit/data/protocols/method) do not, and no doc records that split as a choice — real but cosmetic; the cockpit's missing canonical (89 of 90 have one) is a genuine inconsistency.
findings_confirmed.corrected_root_cause: Two defects, not one: (1) the generator enumerates files rather than the page registry (finder's class, correct), AND (2) url_for() strips .html for non-index files, producing extensionless URLs CloudFront resolves as 301→/…/→404 — so the fragment is not merely indexed, it is a dead sitemap entry that also feeds tests/site_review_bindings._sitemap_routes.

CloudWatch /aws/lambda/life-platform-delete-user-data 2026-08-24 and 2026-08-31 08:00Z 'retention_sweep_complete {mode: anonymize …}'. lambdas/operational/traffic_digest_lambda.py:367-375 oldest_pending computed over every pending_confirmation row. lambdas/web/email_subscriber_lambda.py:514-517 expired tokens are only rejected at confirm time, never transitioned.

findings_confirmed.class: a lifecycle state with no terminal transition — the token expires but the row does not, so the measurement surface built on it (#1954) cannot decay
findings_confirmed.regression_guard: The weekly sweep transitions pending rows past token_expires+7d to status=expired (privacy: email hash only, already the case); aggregate_subscriber_funnel counts expired separately and oldest_pending excludes them; a fixture with an expired pending must show 0 live pendings.
findings_confirmed.blast_radius: The only funnel instrument the platform has reports a permanently stale warning and an inflated pending count — alarm fatigue on the one growth signal.
findings_confirmed.verifier_reason: Reproduced live (read-only DDB query, pk=USER#matthew#SOURCE#subscribers, Count 3): 1 confirmed (2026-03-28), 2 pending_confirmation created 2026-07-03T23:45Z/23:50Z with token_expires 2026-07-05 — 61 days past expiry today. Both pending rows still carry plaintext email (checked as a boolean only: email_present=True, anonymized=False on all 3 rows). Code reproduces: lambdas/content/subscriber_retention.py:44 RETENTION_WINDOW_DAYS = 0, :61 is_retention_eligible requires status == 'unsubscribed' — a pending row is structurally never eligible; lambdas/web/email_subscriber_lambda.py:514-517 rejects an expired token at confirm time but writes no transition. Digest: lambdas/operational/traffic_digest_lambda.py:367-368 oldest_pending scans every pending row, :427-432 renders the '⚠ oldest pending confirmation is N days old — its confirmation link is long expired; the funnel is leaking' block whenever oldest > 7 — so with this DDB state the warning is emitted every Monday by construction and nothing can ever clear it. Could not read the rendered digest from CloudWatch (6 events in /aws/lambda/life-platform-traffic-digest over 21d, 0 carry the funnel dict — the Lambda does not log it), so the live render is inferred from deterministic code + measured state, not observed. Dedup: #1954 (closed 08-02) built the section and its own warning text acknowledges the class but shipped no transition; not in HANDOVER_LATEST (358 lines), not in last 60 closed / 33 open issues. NOT a documented posture: docs/DATA_GOVERNANCE.md:105 (the #3044 SIGNED row) says 'Active (pending/confirmed) subscribers are never touched' with the rationale 'an ongoing delivery relationship is the lawful basis' — that rationale never came into being for a pending whose opt-in token expired 61 days ago, so the posture is shown wrong for this sub-case rather than merely restated. Premise correction: the 7-day new_pending_7d/new_confirmed_7d ratio (:362-365) is windowed and NOT contaminated by these rows; what is contaminated is by_status total, oldest_pending_days, and the permanent warning. Two things the finder missed that raise the weight: (a) privacy — two third-party plaintext emails retained indefinitely under a signed 0-day policy whose text excludes them by category; (b) the fix requires AMENDING the signed governance row (#3044 owner sign-off), not a silent code change.
findings_confirmed.corrected_root_cause: A lifecycle state machine with no terminal transition for pending_confirmation: expiry is checked only on the confirm read path, the sweep's eligibility predicate is status=='unsubscribed' only, and the signed DATA_GOVERNANCE row (#3044) classifies every pending row as 'active' regardless of token state. The permanent digest warning is a symptom; the retained unconfirmed plaintext PII is the larger consequence.
